action: Microsoft says this was not an attack, so no security action is needed. General advice: confirm that delayed email has arrived, check your agreement for service credits and review how staff communicate when email is down.
exec: A prolonged email and collaboration outage shows dependence on one cloud supplier; Microsoft says it was not an attack.
impact: Outlook, Teams and Copilot were disrupted in 74 countries; per CyberCube the broader incident lasted about 38 hours.
plain: A fault on November 12 disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot in 74 countries, per Al Jazeera. Microsoft's report says its testing missed the hardware and traffic mix involved; Microsoft says it was not a cyberattack.

evidence.quote: "Our testing did not adequately represent the combination of hardware and traffic mix encountered during this incident," Microsoft said in the report.
will most likely total less than $100 mn, according to its preliminary catastrophe analysis.

Outlook, Teams and Copilot remain disrupted in 74 countries.
Severe disruption lasted approximately 18 hours, while the overall incident continued for about 38 hours.

summary: Outlook, Teams and Copilot were disrupted from 12 November in 74 countries, per Al Jazeera; CyberCube puts the broader incident at about 38 hours. Microsoft's report says its testing did not adequately represent the hardware and traffic mix encountered (KIRO 7). Cyber Security News says Microsoft declared an internal "Code Red" afterwards, aiming to restore service worldwide within an hour during future incidents.
title: Microsoft outage knocks out Outlook, Teams and Copilot in 74 countries

validation.note: Al Jazeera (13 Nov) and KIRO 7 (21 Nov) each state the outage and Microsoft's statement that it was not a cyberattack; Beinsure relays CyberCube estimates. BleepingComputer returned 403 and Digital Daily failed to load, so neither is cited.
